newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 17.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Feb 17.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:

** Reliance Industries Ltd (RIL) has appointed Deloitte, Touche, Tohmatsu International (DTTI) as its internatinoal accountants. This is the first instance of any Indian company appointing an international accountant, the Economic Times says.

While DTI will assist RIL in adhering to international norms of financial reporting, accounting standards and disclosures, the company's move to appoint the world's fifth largest chartered accountancy firm is seen as a precursor to some major steps that RIL is expected to take in the near future.
Foremost among these is a move to enlist RIL's bonds on the New York Stock Echange as well as other exchanges in the United States like Amex, the paper says.

** India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index rose to 7.73 percent in the week ending February 1 from 7.66 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said on Sunday.
** Volatile Indian stock markets are expected to repeat their traditional pre-budget rally this week, brokers and analysts said at the week-end.

India's Finance Minister P. Chidambaram is scheduled to unveil the federal budget for fiscal 1997/98 (April-March) on February 28. Analysts said expectations of incentives for industry to boost investments in infrastructure ventures like power, roads and ports, where chronic shortages have undermined India's growth, were high.
Last week the Bombay share index jumped 114.77 points, or 3.37 percent, to 3,521.99.
